Method of Attack: Serving malicious JavaScript malware on eFile.com webpages
Loading base64-encoded JavaScript that loads further malware from infoamanewonliag.online
Using Math.random() to prevent caching and ensure fresh malware load
Prompting users to download next stage payload executables (update.exe for Chrome, installer.exe for Firefox) flagged as trojans
Backdoor PHP malware allowing remote command execution and control
Establishing connection to remote command and control server for executing tasks and downloading additional files
Discoverer: Dr. Johannes Ulrich of SANS Institute
Impacted Systems: Windows devices infected by backdoor PHP malware
Attack Vector: Compromise of eFile.com website to serve malicious JavaScript files
Malicious JavaScript loading further payloads from illicit domain infoamanewonliag.online
Social engineering via fake SSL error message to prompt downloads
Delivery of trojan executables via browser-specific prompts
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious JavaScript file 'popper.js' served on eFile.com
Malicious JavaScript file 'update.js' served from Amazon AWS endpoint
Payload executables: update.exe, installer.exe flagged on VirusTotal
Fake SSL error message encoded in base64 within update.js
